comments.author: olooney
comments.story_title: Self Studying the MIT Applied Math Curriculum
comments.why_zh: 加深了对 SVD 等关键概念的理解
comments.quote_zh: 强烈推荐。我本来只是想复习一下，却对几个重要概念有了更深的理解
comments.text_zh: 我毕业几年后学了 Strang 的线性代数课[0]（链接指向 YouTube 上的讲座播放列表），并强烈推荐它。我本来只是想复习一下，却对几个重要概念有了更深的理解；尤其可以说，在 Strang 之前我几乎没弄懂，甚至可能误解了 SVD。如果你不确定自己是否需要这样的课，我建议你用这个视频[1]或 MIT 的习题集[2]自测一下；人很容易对自己说“我懂”线性代数，而更接近事实的说法是：你以前懂过线性代数，但今天连基础问题都答不上来。学完 Strang 之后，Golub 那本 Matrix Computations 也非常了不起。[3] [0]: [VIDEO] [1]: [LINK] [2]: [LINK] [3]: [LINK]
comments.text: I did Strang's linear algebra course[0] (link goes to Youtube playlist of lectures) several years after graduating and recommend it highly. I was looking for refresher but I gained a deeper understanding of several important concepts; in particular it's fair to say I barely understood, or perhaps even misunderstood, SVD until Strang. If you're not sure if you need something like that, I suggest doing something like testing yourself on this video[1] or the MIT problem sets[2] it's easy to tell yourself that you "know" linear algebra when it would be closer to the truth to say that you used to know linear algebra, but can't answer even basic questions today. After Strang, Golub's book on Matrix Computations is also really incredible.[3] [0]: [VIDEO] [1]: [LINK] [2]: [LINK] [3]: [LINK]

comments.text_zh: 我之前在 HN 上提过这个，但我觉得对于想学 ML、又觉得自己数学落后的人来说仍然有用。如果你像我一样，没法坐着啃下大量数学教材，而更喜欢有人通过可以反复回放的视频给你讲解，那么这里有一份课程清单，能把你从基础代数和微积分预备知识一路带到理解最先进 ML 算法背后原理所需的概念。全部由各自领域里精力充沛的专家讲解，而且从最基础开始。涵盖微积分、线性代数、概率、统计、凸优化，还顺手给 HN 读者加了一门 ML 数学课：（前两门是 1970 年代录制的“MOOC”！可能是史上最早的 MOOC 录像，甚至早于互联网，讲师绝对是宝藏）Calculus Revisited: Single Variable Calculus | MIT [LINK] 。Calculus Revisited: Multivariable Calculus | MIT [LINK] 。Complex Variables, Differential Equations, and Linear Algebra | MIT [LINK] 。Linear Algebra | MIT - [VIDEO] 。Introduction to Linear Dynamical Systems |Stanford [LINK] Probability | Harvard [LINK] 。Intermediate Statistics | CMU [LINK] 。Convex Optimization I | Stanford [LINK] Math Background for ML | CMU [LINK] 。

All explained by very energetic people who are experts in their fields, and starting from the very basics. This covers calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, convex optimization and a math for ML course thrown in for the HN audience: (The first two are "MOOCs" recorded in the 1970s! probably the first ever recorded MOOC, even before the internet, and the lecturer is absolute gold) Calculus Revisited: Single Variable Calculus | MIT [LINK] . comments.author: webartifex
comments.story_title: Show HN: Intro to Python and Programming for non-CS majors
comments.why_zh: 想自称数据科学家的人应具备的基础课程
comments.quote_zh: 请确保他们掌握这里（Gilbert Strang 的线性代数课）的全部内容
comments.text_zh: 这取决于谁想雇你。对于顶尖工作，这肯定不够。我总是告诉人们，在声称自己是数据科学家之前，请确保他们掌握这里[VIDEO]（Gilbert Strang 的线性代数课）的全部内容。我敢打赌，我能教会一只猴子用 pandas 打开 CSV 并调用 sklearn 里的 .fit()。但这些人真的理解背后的假设吗？我确信大多数自称数据科学家的人并不理解。我仍然很难把自己称为数据科学家。而我已经读了一个相关领域的博士三年了。我学得越多，越觉得自己真正知道得越少。
comments.text: It depends on who wants to hire you. For the top jobs, this is for sure not enough. I always tell people to please make sure they know all the contents from here [VIDEO] (Gilbert Strang's Linear Algebra course) before they make any claims about being a data scientist. I bet I can teach a monkey to open a CSV in pandas and call .fit() in sklearn. But do the people really understand the underlying assumptions. Most self-proclaimed data scientists don't I am sure. I still have a hard time calling myself a data scientist. And I am three years into a relevant PhD. The more I study, the less I feel I truly know.

comments.author: baby
comments.story_title: LHC Physics Center bans Powerpoint, switches to whiteboard-only forums
comments.text_zh: 我不太理解这一点。我的大多数老师都用黑板，跟着那样的讲解真的很烦，你得等那个人写，课后也没有幻灯片可以辅助你的笔记，而且因为网上没有幻灯片，他们写的所有东西你都得自己抄，结果你甚至没法好好听讲。而且有些东西在幻灯片上就是更清楚……我真没看出纯白板讲课有多少好处。白板和幻灯片结合才是最好的。我也能想到一些不用幻灯片的大牛，但这很少见，只有少数人能做得很好（我想到的是 Gilbert Strang[1]）。[1]: [VIDEO]
comments.text: I don't understand this. Most of my teachers use blackboards and it's really annoying to follow a presentation like that, you have to wait for the person to write, you have no slides later on to support your notes, and since you have no slides online you have to write everything they write, so you can't even listen properly to the talk. And some stuff are just clearer on slides... I don't really see a lot of benefits in whiteboard-only lectures. Combination of whiteboard and slides are best. I can still think of some great people who don't use slides but it's rare and a few people do it well (Gilbert Strang comes to my mind[1]). [1]: [VIDEO]
